## Build and test adoption

BUILD-SPOTBUGS-01/04/05, BUILD-CPD-02, BUILD-DEPS-03 and BUILD-PMD-06 completed
tool adoption and semantic triage. Their current scopes/counts/versions belong
to checked-in POM/build-support inputs and [build-quality](../../docs/dev/build-quality.md),
not historical rollout counts. SpotBugs acceptance must have per-finding rationale;
CPD/PMD counts are reviewed ratchets. Maven dependency analysis remains opt-in
advisory, without broad ignores or failOnWarning. Its initial 14 actionable POM
mismatches included removal of application→platform-errors and CSV→commons-io;
retirement intake must not reopen those resolved edges.

TEST-LIFECYCLE-01, COVERAGE-02, REGEX-03, WAITS-04, EXTERNAL-05, PILOTS-06,
CODECOV-07 and CONSUMERS-09 established the global controls. Per-module review
is separate. The original regex/CSV-metadata intake findings are now resolved;
existing [testing policy](../../docs/TESTING.md) owns the supported contracts.
Required project-owned status-policy activation was qualified in
[run 34679847573](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/actions/runs/34679847573),
not inferred from current local code alone.

Historical diagnostic pilots were report-only weekly/manual adoption:

  about 53 s / 337 MiB peak RSS. Six feature-extractor survivors changed delimiters at

  exact then-current 261-suite union, no automatic retry. This is not today's suite

old-binary downgrade rejection, coordinated rollback, file/JDBC ledgers, managed
import success/quarantine, canonical receipt and ordered names. They did not
switch the root-owned systemd service. Implementation gate `3825523a` passed the
then-current verify/PMD scopes; its offline Dependency-Check 129/zero result did
not refresh NVD and is not current security evidence.

`docs/quality`, clean at entry. The only production change in this slice removes
the unused internal `StableArtifactId` record; library implementations, POMs,
analyzer policies, accepted findings and coverage/test ratchets are unchanged.
This is module-scope credit, not application release/security qualification.

Production Java, package Javadoc, module POM/resources and test inventories were
compared, including package-private collaborators. Shared parent properties are
unchanged against the last five library sources; concurrency's earlier parent
changes concern the application stack, not its zero-dependency production API.
Current architecture tests enforce JDK-only, SLF4J-only or Spring-facing limits;
their cycle rule checks top-level ownership/platform subsystems, not every
subpackage. Diagnostics result/sink depend on its root model. Logging has a
root↔ecs package cycle: `LogEvent` uses ECS descriptors/outcomes and `EcsFields`
uses root `LogFieldSpec`/`LogValueType`. `ARCH-LOG-1` accepts this coupling within
one published artifact: the descriptor types do not depend on `LogEvent`, and
both directions belong to one typed logging contract, not separate ownership.
The logging maintainer reopens it if ECS becomes independently reusable or a
dependency crosses the library boundary. Redaction is JDK-only; the other four
libraries have one production package. No relocation is required for this scope.

Retirement disposition is `keep-supported` for the published APIs, their
package-private implementation helpers, no-ops and compatibility behavior.
No new remove-now candidate was established in these six scopes. Finite
observer/error/order/ownership/capacity checks from their named reviews remain
valid for unchanged implementation; deterministic suites recheck integration
with today's reactor. This closes 24 module cells, with DOC already verified.

TOOL-6/7/8/9, another deployed consumer, live endpoints, other framework/provider
baselines and current security scans are not closed by this credit. Repository
consumers and signed RC files were not republished or requalified remotely.
The other 20 module reviews remain open; DATA, regex, TCK and global test/build
outcomes are reusable scoped evidence, not automatic whole-module passes.

### Internal retirement

`RETIRE-APP-11` removes
`com.iocextractor.application.artifact.StableArtifactId` and its obsolete package
README entry. At input HEAD, an all-tracked byte search found only the record,
README and two roadmap references. Production source/resource/metadata inspection
found no dynamic class loading, serialization or SPI consumer for it. The
application module is internal and is not one of the six published coordinates;
their source/archive scopes exclude it. Public visibility alone did not create
a supported standalone application SDK.

The record held no validation, allocator, persistence mapping or caller behavior.
Canonical/lifecycle IDs, export slots, SQL migrations and public CSV/manifest
formats are unchanged. A clean rebuild prevents stale bytecode from concealing
the removal; application tests protect the supported neighboring behavior.
This closes the named candidate, not the complete application retirement census.

### Remaining review and verification boundary

All 26 module POMs, source/test inventories and owning reading maps were
reconciled. The remaining 20 need their module-specific behavior/resource/
visibility/retirement checks; the existing DATA/regex/global controls are credited
within their original scope. Current CPD/PMD membership has 22 groups/19 policy
findings; retained historical semantic items are not a complete current census.
Additional occurrences now have owner/disposition in the execution contract;
no count, rule, suppression or coverage baseline changes to obtain a pass.

`QUAL-BOOT-1` remains open: 134 source files share the composition package.
Configuration, processing, storage, lifecycle, import, sync/export and health
are candidate package slices. `ProcessingPolicyFingerprint.addValue` currently
hashes record FQCN/component identity, so relocating configuration records can
change durable policy identity with unchanged YAML. Preserve those names until
independent fingerprint/restart characterization and an explicit compatibility
decision precede any move. This is a relocation constraint, not a newly observed
runtime defect or authority to change the fingerprint algorithm.

Verification for this slice uses `./mvnw -B -ntp clean`, focused application tests,
then `make verify`, separate `make pmd-analysis`, `make docs` and
`git diff --check` on the completed worktree. Check removal from main classes,
sources and the rebuilt application JAR as well as source-level absence.
The full gates establish deterministic current-source acceptance; they do not
renew earlier stand/resource/repository/security measurements. Local raw results
are retained under `.dev/module-hardening-reconciliation/` and freshness receipts
under `.dev/state/`; failed/unavailable commands must be reported independently.

### Maintainer scope decision — 2026-11-17

The maintainer explicitly deferred remediation of OPS-10, OPS-12 and OPS-15 to
later releases. Their fixes are outside the 0.3.0 execution baseline; the entries
remain open with impact, operational restrictions and regression acceptance in
[KNOWN-ISSUES](../../docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md). This is a scope decision, not a fixed
defect, a new test pass or deferral of every OPS issue. Candidate notes preserve
the accepted residual risks. QUAL/TEST/REL consume this named exception.

Further code review identified direct assembly calls from router/import
configuration into `AppConfig`, repeated JDBC schema/header knowledge and
lifecycle artifact-catalog validation. Proposed refactoring slices preserve
fingerprint/FQCN, resource ownership and transaction/recovery semantics. Their
implementation is not claimed here; QUAL-BOOT-1 remains open.

### Structural refactoring deferral — 2026-11-18

The maintainer explicitly moved the proposed architectural/technical refactoring
outside 0.3.0 because implementation and requalification would expand this
release substantially. `QUAL-BOOT-1` changes from `fix-now` to `deferred`;
bootstrap assembly/package moves, catalog/shutdown/logging/CSV consolidation,
constructor changes and durable-workflow decomposition are future work.
Permanent [ARCH-6](../../docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md#arch-6) and
[CODE-6](../../docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md#code-6) preserve concrete coupling/duplication,
fingerprint and ownership risks, responsible capabilities and return/acceptance
criteria without promising a future version. The baseline, goals, matrix and
candidate notes consume this accepted exception. This does not claim debt closure,
change the six credited module scopes or waive remaining review/dispositions,
security obligations or final candidate gates. No production code or gate policy
changed for this decision.


### Repository controls and security scheduling — 2026-11-20

Scope: the maintainer accepted PRs with blocking CI and zero required reviewers,
explicit publication approval, release-branch safeguards and component-tag
protection. This review used source HEAD
`202cb3345c6ea37c08c915816028c8c2ae684f69` with uncommitted changes; it is not a
clean candidate qualification or a new vulnerability/stand result.

- [Branch ruleset 27737840](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/rules/27737840)
  is active on `main` and all `release-*`, without bypass actors: PRs, strict
  GitHub Actions `build`/`packaging-contracts`/`doc-links`, no force-push/delete.
  Creation is allowed before initial checks. Existing classic protections and
  the two additional 0.3.0 checks remain. Effective-rule GETs covered `main`,
  `release-0.3.0`, future `release-0.4.0` and excluded `docs/quality`; no test refs
  were created or pushed.
- [Tag ruleset 19423734](https://github.com/xORex-LC/ioc-extractor/rules/19423734)
  covers `v*` and all six admitted component prefixes. Administrator bypass
  remains, as recorded in policy. No existing tag or published byte changed.
- GitHub Actions `sha_pinning_required=true` was read back after activation.
  Supported `main`/0.2.0/0.3.0 workflow refs were inspected beforehand and used
  full-SHA Action references; default token permissions remain read-only.
- `SECURITY CHECKS` allows `main`/`release-*` without reviewer approval.
  Publication-environment settings and NVD secret metadata were preserved.
  Current secret scanning/push protection are enabled; registry/threat claims
  were corrected without claiming a complete historical secrets audit.
- Editable [control requests](../repository-controls/README.md) record the desired
